title: SaaS Pricing Drift: A Verification Framework for Buyers
description: A transparent method for checking whether published SaaS prices are current. This is a verification framework, not a completed market-wide price audit; claims without dated primary evidence remain unverified.
keyFindings: Pricing comparisons are only meaningful when product, plan, region, currency, billing cadence and usage unit match.
A discrepancy requires a preserved published claim and a current official vendor source checked on a recorded date.
A headline subscription amount may omit seats, usage limits, onboarding, integrations, support or renewal terms.
Unverified or quote-only prices should be labeled as such rather than converted into a numeric estimate.
A reproducible audit needs source links, capture dates, inclusion rules, exclusions and a calculation method.

sections.title: Why pricing drift matters
sections.body: A comparison can mislead buyers if it repeats a discontinued plan, confuses monthly and annual billing or omits a required add-on. The risk is especially high when vendors price by seats, usage, region or negotiated contract. This report does not claim that a market-wide sample has been completed; it explains how to verify a claim before publishing it.

sections.title: Evidence standard
sections.body: Record the exact third-party claim and the official vendor source checked on a stated date. Match the product, plan, currency, country, billing interval, unit and included limits. Preserve a source snapshot where permitted. If the official source is unavailable or the vendor uses quote-only pricing, mark the value unverified rather than guessing.

sections.title: Patterns to investigate
sections.body: Common audit targets include annual-versus-monthly price differences, minimum seat commitments, included usage, add-on fees, changed plan names, regional differences, promotional offers and renewal uplifts. These are patterns to check, not claims that a particular vendor currently has an error. Keep observations separate from conclusions until the evidence is comparable.

sections.title: Repeatable verification procedure
sections.body: For each claim, save the page URL, access date, product and plan, region, currency, billing term, user or usage unit, included features and any stated exclusions. Ask the vendor for a dated quote if a required detail is missing. Have a second reviewer confirm the comparison before publishing a numeric discrepancy.

sections.title: Calculate buyer impact
sections.body: Normalize the figures to the same billing period and unit. For a per-seat difference, multiply by the actual seat count and number of billing periods, then list add-ons and usage charges separately. State assumptions and do not extrapolate a negotiated quote to all customers. If the plan scope differs, report the comparison as not like-for-like.

sections.title: Limitations and updates
sections.body: Prices can vary by contract, region, promotions and negotiated terms. One observation does not establish an industry-wide trend. A future quantitative report should publish the sample frame, observation dates, source links, inclusion rules, exclusions and calculation code. Until that evidence exists, this page remains a methodology guide and does not claim a completed pricing-drift measurement.

methodology: No market-wide vendor-price sample is claimed as completed. For each future audited observation, record the exact third-party claim, current official vendor URL, date accessed, region, currency, plan, billing cadence, usage unit, included features and exclusions. Mark quote-only or unavailable values unverified. Only calculate a discrepancy when the two observations are comparable and reproducible.
dataSources: Official vendor pricing pages and product documentation (to be recorded per observation)
Dated vendor quotes where public prices are unavailable (retain scope and region)
Published comparison claims under review (record exact URL and capture date)
author: Emily Nakamura

faqs.question: Does this report prove that SaaS prices have increased?
faqs.answer: No. It is a verification framework, not a completed market-wide study. Quantitative claims require a documented sample and comparable dated primary sources.

faqs.question: What counts as evidence of a price change?
faqs.answer: A dated prior claim and a current official vendor source for the same product, plan, region, currency, billing term and unit. If those do not match, the difference may not represent a true price change.

faqs.question: What if the vendor does not publish a price?
faqs.answer: Mark the price quote-based or unverified and request a written quote. Do not invent a number or infer one from an unrelated plan.

faqs.question: How often should a pricing page be reviewed?
faqs.answer: Set a review cadence based on how frequently the category changes and recheck before publishing a specific price. Record the date and source for every claim.
